name: Alamocita
remarks: Town was abandoned in 1880, due to change in the course of the Rio Grande, some ranches remained. Site was submerged by the Elephant Butte Reservoir.

name: Aleman
remarks: Buildings on the Bar Cross Ranch

name: Anaconda
remarks: A former mining town that also once contained the only medical facility between Albuquerque and Gallup.

name: Arkansas Junction
remarks: Not much is left of the former community except a cafe that serves the local oil field workers.

name: Baldy Town
remarks: The site is part of the Philmont Boy Scout Ranch. It has stone ruins and mill foundations which are a part of historic programming.

name: Bland
remarks: Destroyed in the 2011 Las Conchas Fire, some foundations remain.

name: Cabezon
remarks: Private property. Several structures remain.

name: Cambray
remarks: Private property. Structures remain in various states of disrepair.

name: Canta Recio
remarks: Site was submerged by the Elephant Butte Reservoir.

name: Chise
remarks: Populated Place.

name: Chloride
remarks: An unincorporated community

name: Cuchillo
remarks: An unincorporated community. Name change came after the 1900 Census, it was recorded under its present name in the 1910 Census.

name: Dawson
remarks: Once Large City, suffered two major mining incidents totaling some 400 casualties, Phelps Dodge Company cleared the town of relics and infrastructure

name: Elizabethtown
remarks: Once largest town in New Mexico. Ruins of one stone structure is all that remains, most wooden structures lost in 1903 fire.

name: Endee
remarks: Founded as a supply center for ranches in the area.

name: Glenrio
county: Quay (partially in Deaf Smith County, Texas)

name: Gran Quivira
remarks: (now part of the Salinas Pueblo Missions National Monument)

name: Hermosa
remarks: Mostly private property, but several structures remain. Ranch is owned by Ted Turner.

name: Jicarilla
remarks: Half a dozen structures remain at the site, including both former schoolhouses.

name: Kelly
remarks: Founded in 1866 after Patrick H. Kelly staked lead, Zinc and silver; mining sustained the town until prices declined. Small population and guided tours remain.

name: La Belle
remarks: The town was founded as a result of a gold mine and ceased when the mining ended.

name: Mentmore
remarks: (still has post office and zip code 87319)

name: Montoya
remarks: Originally founded as a railroad stop in 1902. A Sinclair gasoline station operated from 1925 to the mid-1970s.

name: Newkirk
remarks: In the 2010 census, Newkirk had a population of 7.

name: Old Hachita
remarks: Several structures remain, including mine headframes.

name: Paraje
remarks: Site was submerged by the Elephant Butte Reservoir. Later exposed, some ruins and artifacts can be seen.

name: Pinos Altos (High Pines)
remarks: Still has some people there, located near Silver City

name: Santa Barbara
remarks: The village was abandoned in 1851 because of Apache raids and in 1860 by a Navajo raid. It was not re-occupied until 1875 and was renamed as Hatch.

name: San Albino
remarks: Site was submerged by the Elephant Butte Reservoir.

name: San José
remarks: Site was submerged by the Elephant Butte Reservoir.

name: San Marcial
remarks: Destroyed by flood 1866, rebuilt on opposite bank of the Rio Grande, destroyed by flood in 1929 and abandoned.

name: San Ygnacio de la Alamosa
remarks: Abandoned after destruction by flooding in 1867. Site was submerged by the Elephant Butte Reservoir.

name: Santa Rita
remarks: Town site swallowed up by the open pit copper mine several times.

name: Shakespeare
remarks: Currently part of a privately owned ranch, sometimes open to tourists.

name: Twining
remarks: (site of Taos Ski Valley)

name: Vinegaroon
remarks: (east of La Luz, New Mexico; at the mouth of La Borcita)

name: Zapata
remarks: Site was submerged by the Elephant Butte Reservoir.
